docs.text:
• mkdocs new [dir-name] - Create a new project.
  • mkdocs serve - Start the live-reloading docs server.
  • mkdocs build - Build the documentation site.
  • mkdocs -h - Print help message and exit.

docs.title: Keithley IV Measurement GUI User Manual
Model Selection
docs.text:
• Choose between Keithley 2400 (GPIB 1) or Keithley 2401 (GPIB 2)
  • 2400: Voltage range up to 200V
  • 2401: Voltage range up to 20V

docs.title: 1. Source Mode
docs.text:
• Voltage Source: For standard IV measurements (most common)
  • You control voltage, measure current
  • Current Source: For specialized measurements
  • You control current, measure voltage

docs.title: 2. Range Settings
docs.text: Important: Ranges and compliance values are interdependent!

docs.title: For Voltage Source Mode:
docs.text:
1. Voltage Range 2401: 0.2V, 2V, 20V 2400: 0.2V, 2V, 20V, 200V
  2. Choose the smallest range that covers your sweep range

  3. Must be ≥ your maximum sweep voltage

  4. Current Range Options: 1µA, 10µA, 100µA, 1mA, 10mA, 100mA, 1A

  5. Must be ≥ your current compliance

  6. Choose based on expected current

  7. Compliance Settings

  8. Current Compliance must be ≤ Current Range
  9. Voltage Compliance should be ≥ Voltage Range

docs.title: For Current Source Mode:
docs.text:
1. Current Range
  2. Must be ≥ your maximum sweep current

  3. Choose the smallest range that covers your sweep range

  4. Voltage Range

  5. Must be ≥ your voltage compliance
  6. 2401: Max 20V
  7. 2400: Max 200V

docs.title: 3. Sweep Parameters
docs.text:
1. Start and Stop Values
  2. Must be within your selected voltage/current range

  3. Example: For 2V range, keep within ±2V

  4. Number of Steps Recommended: 100-1000 points More points = smoother curve but longer measurement

  5. Delay Minimum: 0.1s recommended Increase for high-impedance measurements

  6. Too short: noisy data

  7. Too long: very slow measurement

  8. NPLC (Number of Power Line Cycles) 0.01: Fastest, noisiest 1.0: Good balance (recommended) 10.0: Slowest, lowest noise

docs.title: For Most IV Measurements:
docs.text:
Start with:
- Voltage Source Mode
- 2V Voltage Range
- 10mA Current Range
- 10mA Current Compliance
- 1.0 NPLC
- 0.1s Delay
- 100 steps

docs.title: Then adjust based on your device:
docs.text:
• High resistance: ↑ Increase voltage range ↓ Decrease current compliance
  • Low resistance: ↓ Decrease voltage range ↑ Increase current compliance

docs.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid:
docs.text:
1. Setting compliance higher than range
  2. Setting sweep values outside the selected range
  3. Using too short delay times
  4. Setting current compliance too high for sensitive devices

docs.title: Safety Tips:
docs.text:
• [ ] Always start with conservative compliance values
  • [ ] Verify settings before connecting device
  • [ ] Monitor the first few measurements for compliance issues

docs.title: Compliance Errors:
docs.text:
Check:
✓ Is sweep range within voltage range?
✓ Is current compliance appropriate?
✓ Are ranges properly set for compliance values?

docs.title: Noisy Data:
docs.text:
Try:
✓ Increase NPLC
✓ Increase delay time
✓ Use smaller ranges if possible
✓ Check shielding/grounding

docs.title: No Measurements:
docs.text:
Verify:
✓ GPIB addresses match instruments
✓ All connections are secure
✓ Output is enabled
✓ Compliance settings aren't too restrictive

Note: This manual assumes basic familiarity with electrical measurements and Keithley instruments.

docs.title: Windows Setup
docs.text: Yes, the Shift key method is a more thorough way to ensure a complete shutdown. Let me update the instructions:

docs.title: Required: Disable Fast Startup
docs.text:
Fast Startup must be disabled for proper GPIB device detection. Follow these steps:

  1. Open Control Panel
  2. Go to Power Options
  3. Click Choose what the power buttons do
  4. Click Change settings that are currently unavailable
  5. Uncheck ✓ Turn on fast startup (recommended)
  6. Click Save changes

docs.title: Proper Shutdown Procedure
docs.text:
After disabling Fast Startup, perform a full shutdown:

  1. Save all work
  2. Hold down Shift key
  3. Click Start Menu → Power → Shut Down
  4. Keep holding Shift until screen goes black
  5. Wait 30 seconds after shutdown
  6. Power on your computer
  7. Wait for full boot-up
  8. Connect to Keithley instruments

Important: The Shift key method forces Windows to perform a complete shutdown instead of a hybrid shutdown, ensuring all devices are properly reinitialized on next boot.

Note: These settings may need to be checked again after Windows updates.
